title: Self-Assessment
intro: This is a reflection on where you are today. There are no right or wrong answers.
Your responses are designed to help you recognize strengths, identify areas for growth, and measure your progress over time.

Use a simple 1–5 scale:
1 — Rarely | 2 — Sometimes | 3 — Developing | 4 — Usually | 5 — Consistently
safety_note: If anything here doesn't feel safe to answer, you can step away at any time. Your safety and your child's safety come first.
resume_message: Welcome back. Let's pick up where you left off.

sections.title: My Focus on My Child
questions: I keep my child's needs at the center of my decisions.
I can separate my feelings about the other parent from my child's relationship with them.
I consider how conflict between parents may affect my child.
I listen for what my child may need rather than asking them to choose sides.
I can identify what my child needs from me right now.

sections.title: My Self-Awareness
questions: I recognize when my emotions are affecting how I respond.
I can identify situations that trigger conflict for me.
I take responsibility for my own words and actions.
I can recognize when I need time before responding.
I am willing to consider another perspective even when I disagree.

sections.title: My Communication
questions: I communicate about our child without unnecessary criticism or blame.
I can keep messages focused on the issue that needs to be addressed.
I avoid responding immediately when I am angry or upset.
I can communicate clearly about schedules, school, health, and other child-related needs.
I try to communicate in ways that reduce rather than increase conflict.

sections.title: My Ability to Work Through Differences
questions: I can distinguish between an important parenting issue and a personal disagreement.
I can identify areas where the other parent and I already agree.
I am willing to consider more than one solution to a parenting problem.
I can compromise when doing so supports my child's needs.
When we cannot agree, I can seek appropriate help rather than allowing the conflict to escalate.

reflection.title: My Progress
reflection.intro: Now let's shift away from ratings and make this genuinely reflective. Write as much or as little as you like — or skip any question.

questions.prompt: What is going better in your co-parenting relationship than it was before?
What is one thing you have done differently that has helped your child?
What is one communication habit you would like to improve?
What is one goal you want to work on before your next Self-Assessment?

goal.prompt: What would you like to work on next?
goal.label: Personal Co-Parenting Goal
goal.helper: Your answer becomes your Personal Co-Parenting Goal. It stays on your dashboard until your next Self-Assessment.

completion_message: Thank you for taking the time to reflect. Here's where you are today.

chart.title: Your Progress Over Time
chart.first_note: This is your starting point. Your next Self-Assessment will show how each area has changed.

central_message: Your progress isn't about changing the other parent. It's about recognizing what you can do to create a healthier co-parenting environment for your child.

bands.label: Consistent Strength
bands.body: This is a real strength. Keep protecting it — it's making a difference for your child.

bands.label: Growing Strength
bands.body: You're building solid habits here. Small, steady steps will keep this growing.

bands.label: Developing
bands.body: You're making real progress. Focusing here next could make co-parenting feel calmer.

bands.label: Building Foundations
bands.body: You're laying important groundwork. Every small change you practise counts.

bands.label: Starting Point
bands.body: Every journey starts somewhere. Noticing where you are today is a meaningful first step.

disclaimer: This is a reflection tool — not a diagnosis or custody evaluation.
